- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or neutral (0.0), model often overreacts to recent spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75.00) — apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above 74.00 and true outcome is below 72.00, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1.5–2.5% from next forecast.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.6, -0.3, +0.6), model exhibits lagged response — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day sentiment trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently forecasts >75.00 when true outcome is ≤72.00, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 30d window.
